reason: The cited evidence supports L1₂ precipitation and ~200 MPa yield strength increase in Al0.7CoCrFeNi, but the hypothesis extends this to a different alloy (AlCoCrFeNi₂.1) and claims benefits for creep and corrosion resistance, which are not addressed in the cited passages.
premises: Low-temperature annealing of Al0.7CoCrFeNi induces coherent L1₂ precipitates in the fcc phase
These L1₂ precipitates increase yield strength by ~200 MPa via Orowan mechanism
The strengthening does not severely degrade ductility (elongation remains ~13%)
The same precipitation behavior and strengthening will occur in AlCoCrFeNi₂.1 under similar treatment
L1₂ precipitates will also improve creep and corrosion resistance
